candidates.attacker_control: Content processed by HTMLCleaner that contains HTML comments. A user who can inject HTML/wiki content with a comment such as --> can cause a DOM Comment node whose data contains the comment-terminating sequence "--!>" (and/or "-->"). That comment text is preserved (non-restricted cleaning) and passed to HTMLUtils.toString / XWikiXMLOutputter. In this repository, the HTML diff manager cleans and then serializes with HTMLUtils.toString(htmlDoc) (UnifiedHTMLDiffManager.cleanHTML lines 112-121), and the rendered document HTML that is diffed/displayed is influenced by wiki page content.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Comments are omitted entirely when cleaning is restricted (DefaultHTMLCleaner lines 274-279), so the primary untrusted-content cleaning path is NOT affected; the sanitizer filter (SanitizerFilter) also only runs in restricted mode. The in-repo reachable caller that keeps comments is the XML/HTML diff path (UnifiedHTMLDiffManager.cleanHTML -> HTMLUtils.toString) and other callers may live in xwiki-platform (out of scope). HTMLCleaner may itself reject or truncate some malformed comments, so the attacker's ability to obtain comment text containing "--!>" was not verified at runtime. Whether the missing lines existed in upstream 14.10.3 (i.e. whether this snapshot is the pre-fix state rather than normal upstream behavior) could not be verified without upstream data.
candidates.impact: HTML/DOM injection leading to cross-site scripting (session/CSRF-token theft, actions as the victim) in any rendering path that cleans HTML with comments retained and serializes it with HTMLUtils.toString (the in-repo HTML diff path being a concrete caller). If only trusted/admin content can reach non-restricted cleaning, impact is limited to defense-in-depth and comment-parser confusion rather than direct unprivileged XSS.
candidates.prerequisites: The HTML must be cleaned without the RESTRICTED parameter (so comments survive: DefaultHTMLCleaner only sets omitComments when restricted=true) and then serialized via HTMLUtils.toString/XWikiXMLOutputter while comment nodes are still present; the resulting HTML must be served to another user. Restricted-mode cleaning (used for the main untrusted HTML macro path) drops comments and therefore blocks this specific vector.
candidates.root_cause: XWikiXMLOutputter.printComment (xwiki-commons-xml/src/main/java/org/xwiki/xml/html/HTMLUtils.java lines 184-198) documents the HTML requirement that comment text must not start with ">" or "->", must not contain "<!--", "-->" or "--!>", and must not end with "<!-". The implementation only implements the first requirement (the while loop at lines 193-195 stripping leading ">"/"->"). It never removes/escapes the "<!--", "-->" and "--!>" sequences nor a trailing "<!-". HTMLCleaner keeps comment nodes by default (comments are only omitted when the cleaner is invoked in restricted mode: DefaultHTMLCleaner.getDefaultCleanerProperties, lines 274-279, setOmitComments(isRestricted(configuration))), so comment text that violates the HTML comment grammar can reach the serializer and be emitted verbatim as "<!--" + text + "-->".
candidates.title: Incomplete HTML comment neutralization in HTMLUtils.XWikiXMLOutputter.printComment (comment breakout / markup injection)
candidates.trace: Attacker-controlled wiki/HTML content with a crafted comment -> HTMLCleaner (Comments kept because configuration has no RESTRICTED parameter; UnifiedHTMLDiffManager.cleanHTML sets only USE_CHARACTER_REFERENCES and HTML_VERSION) -> DOM Comment node whose character data contains "--!>"/"-->" -> HTMLUtils.toString(Document) -> XWikiXMLOutputter.printComment strips only leading '>'/'->' and calls JDOM super.printComment, which writes "<!--" + commentText + "-->" (lines 193-197) -> browser parses the comment as ending at the embedded "--!>"/"-->" -> remaining attacker-controlled text after the sequence is parsed as live HTML markup (e.g. an element with a script/event handler) -> script execution in the victim's session.
candidates.unverified: Not runtime-confirmed. HTMLCleaner 2.24's exact comment tokenization of "--!>" and trailing "<!-" was not executed. The exact upstream baseline for this method (whether the removal/escaping of "<!--|-->|--!>" and the trailing "<!-" cleanup were part of 14.10.3 or were removed in this snapshot) could not be checked. End-to-end reachability by an unprivileged user depends on xwiki-platform rendering configuration (not present in this snapshot).
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-79 / CWE-116: improper neutralization of input written into HTML comments (HTML/JS injection via comment termination)

coverage_summary: Coverage: 1,424 files exposed by get_source_scope (all main sources and build files; no src/test trees, no .git metadata). I inventoried all 114 module POMs and read targeted files across xwiki-commons-xml (HTMLCleaner, SecureHTMLElementSanitizer, HTMLUtils, XMLUtils, LocalEntityResolver, SVG/MathML definitions, filters), xwiki-commons-velocity (SecureIntrospector/Uberspector, config, parse-location handler), xwiki-commons-crypto (cipher/password/pkix/signer/store), xwiki-commons-extension (serializer, local storage, repository HTTP/maven/xwiki, job history, XStream utilities), xwiki-commons-filter-xml (XStream parameter manager, XML parser/serializer), xwiki-commons-job (status store, serializer, safe script wrappers), xwiki-commons-netflux, xwiki-commons-classloader, xwiki-commons-environment, xwiki-commons-configuration, xwiki-commons-logging tail, xwiki-commons-diff (incl. diff-xml), xwiki-commons-properties, xwiki-commons-ws and core component/context/cache modules. Search-driven sweeps covered deserialization, URL/SSRF, file/path handling, XML parser configuration, random/hash primitives, reflection and Velocity/script sandbox patterns. Not every one of the 1,424 files was read line-by-line. No code, tests, scanners or network access were executed.
limitations: No upstream baseline or patch data is available in this run, so I could not confirm which of the suspicious spots is a modification versus original 14.10.3 code.
No runtime execution: HTMLCleaner comment tokenization, sanitizer defaults and any exploitability were reasoned statically only.
Reachability of the HTML diff/rendering paths that keep comments is partly implemented in xwiki-platform (not part of this snapshot).
Candidate status is a lead, not a confirmed vulnerability; the report intentionally submits only one candidate and lists the other plausible issues as unconfirmed rejected leads.

rejected_leads.lead: HTMLElementSanitizerConfiguration.isAllowUnknownProtocols() defaults to Boolean.TRUE (xwiki-commons-xml/src/main/java/org/xwiki/xml/internal/html/HTMLElementSanitizerConfiguration.java:132-135), which makes SecureHTMLElementSanitizer's URI allow-list (IS_ALLOWED_URI) ineffective by default (SecureHTMLElementSanitizer.java:196-209).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible insecure-default weakening (only script/data-like schemes remain blocked), but it requires external knowledge of the intended default; nothing in the snapshot states the default should be false, and no concrete script-executing URI scheme survives the \w+script|data: guard. Kept as an unconfirmed lead rather than the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Netflux channel/user keys are generated with java.util.Random (xwiki-commons-core/xwiki-commons-netflux/src/main/java/org/xwiki/netflux/internal/Utils.java:40-48) although Channel.key (Channel.java:36) is a bearer key that grants access to a collaboration channel.
rejected_leads.reason: Non-cryptographic PRNG used for security-relevant keys, but each call creates a fresh Random seeded from nanoTime/uniquifier, so practical prediction of another channel's 48-hex key is not established from source alone; may well be upstream design.

rejected_leads.lead: Unrestricted XStream deserialization: SafeXStream.initialize explicitly skips XStream's security framework (xwiki-commons-xstream/src/main/java/org/xwiki/xstream/internal/SafeXStream.java:83-86), and ParameterXStream/XStreamParameterManager unmarshal filter XML with no type permissions (xwiki-commons-filter-xml/.../ParameterXStream.java, XStreamParameterManager.java:110-128); DefaultXMLParser even reads a class name from XML attribute 't' and calls Class.forName (DefaultXMLParser.java:364-372).
rejected_leads.reason: High-impact class of issue (RCE/DoS), but the permissive setup is an explicit, documented upstream trade-off (FIXME comment) and the attacker-controlled routes (job status/history files, XAR-import XML) are not established within this snapshot; not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: DefaultExtensionSerializer parses extension descriptors with an unhardened DocumentBuilderFactory (xwiki-commons-extension/.../DefaultExtensionSerializer.java:210,284-301), and XMLUtils.parse probes XXE-related Xerces parameters but explicitly sets the disallow-doctype-decl feature to false (xwiki-commons-xml/src/main/java/org/xwiki/xml/XMLUtils.java:606-626).
rejected_leads.reason: External entities are disabled via the external-general/parameter-entity and load-external-dtd features, so this is not a straightforward XXE; for extension descriptors the parser hardening status could not be compared against upstream and remote-descriptor delivery requires a malicious/misconfigured repository.

rejected_leads.lead: SecureIntrospector whitelists 'getclass' for File objects in Velocity (xwiki-commons-velocity/.../SecureIntrospector.java:75-108).
rejected_leads.reason: Gives scripts a Class object, but the whitelisted Class methods (getName, isArray, etc.) do not provide forName/getClassLoader/newInstance, so no RCE chain is visible in the snapshot.

summary: Reviewed the XWiki Commons 14.10.3 source snapshot (1,424 readable files; no test trees present; build/CI files, all main-source modules of xwiki-commons-core and xwiki-commons-tools inspected at least by index and targeted reads). I focused on security-relevant code paths: HTML cleaning/serialization and the secure sanitizer (xwiki-commons-xml), the Velocity sandbox (xwiki-commons-velocity), crypto verification (crypto-pkix/password/signer), extension descriptors and job/XStream serialization, filter XML parsing, netflux real-time keys, classloader URL handling, and environment/configuration resource access. The strongest source-visible issue is an incomplete implementation of the documented HTML-comment sanitization in HTMLUtils.XWikiXMLOutputter.printComment: the method's own comment states comment text must not contain "<!--", "-->", "--!>" nor end with "<!-", but the code only strips leading ">" / "->". Cleaned HTML that still contains comments (comments are only dropped in "restricted" cleaning) can therefore be serialized with a raw "--!>"/"-->" inside a comment, allowing early comment termination and injection of following markup. This is a lead, not a runtime-confirmed vulnerability; reachability on the platform side (non-restricted cleaning paths such as the HTML diff that calls HTMLUtils.toString) and HTMLCleaner's comment parsing were not executed or verified.
